upstream.name: GitoxideLabs/gitoxide
upstream.architecture: Rust workspace for Git object database, packfiles, refs, protocol, worktree, and plumbing crates.

benchmarkDenominator.runner: cargo test workspace and crate-level tests
benchmarkDenominator.runnerStatus: not executed; the upstream cache is sparse/no-checkout and a Cargo run would require materializing crate source plus building Rust workspace dependencies. Full cargo test would also hydrate/build beyond the current VM cap, so this run used targeted static inventory only.
benchmarkDenominator.warning: This is stronger than the seed manifest and now includes targeted object/ref plus focused loose-ref, packed-ref, reference-store overlay, pack-index, pack-data/delta, pack generation, thin/ref-delta generation, object-database, alternates, replacements, multi-pack-index, protocol v2, fetch negotiation, fetch response/sideband, partial clone/promisor, sparse checkout/pathspec, lazy promisor hydration, push request, push response, send-pack orchestration, receive-pack stream transport, git-daemon receive-pack service requests, smart HTTP receive-pack discovery/posting, smart HTTP auth/session header and cookie propagation, safe initial smart HTTP redirect handling, SSH receive-pack URL/command boundary mapping, merge primitive, blob merge, recursive content-merge mapping, bounded merge-index/worktree conflict views, Git index v2 blob-stage writes, tree-stage expansion for directory-file index conflicts, checkout-clean merged worktree writes, merged worktree marker-file writes, directory-file conflict classification, exact same-object rename conflict detection, bounded similar-blob rename conflict detection, same-target rename content merges, bounded directory rename/modify merges, and directory rename matching across renamed internal plugin files, but it is still not upstream pass parity. Next slice should add HTTP proxy/credential-helper behavior, broader directory rename cases, or further rename heuristics.

nativeImplementation.currentSlice: Native loose Git object storage, canonical commit header parsing, Git tree entry parsing/serialization, merge-base ancestry traversal, flat and recursive tree three-way merge decisions, exact same-object rename/delete and rename/rename conflict detection plus bounded similar-blob rename/delete, rename/modify, same-target rename content merges, and directory rename/modify merges with ambiguity guards plus directory rename heuristics across renamed internal plugin files, recursive blob-content merging with conflict-marker blob output, merge-index stage views plus Git index v2 writes for ancestor/ours/theirs blob conflict entries, tree-stage expansion into file-level index entries for directory-file conflicts, checkout-clean merged worktree writes that remove stale files/directories while preserving .git metadata, conflict marker-file writes for content conflicts, directory-file conflict classification, loose direct/symbolic reference parsing and storage, packed-ref header/reference/peeled lookup parsing, protocol v2 capability, ls-refs parsing, fetch feature negotiation and argument building, common fetch filter specs, sparse checkout cone/non-cone path matching, lazy promisor object resolver hydration, fetch response section parsing, sideband pack/progress/error decoding, protocol v1 receive-pack push request building, generated non-delta pack handoff, REF_DELTA pack generation, thin send-pack request building, stream-backed, git-daemon, smart HTTP auth/session/redirect, and SSH receive-pack transport boundaries, report-status parsing, receive-pack advertisement parsing, send-pack session orchestration, loose+packed reference-store overlay resolution, v2 pack-index parsing/lookup, multi-pack-index parsing/lookup, MIDX-backed object database pack selection/de-duplication, pack data entry decoding, OFS_DELTA/REF_DELTA object resolution, and pack+loose+alternate+promisor object database lookup/prefix/iteration with replacement refs.

wordpressScenario: Git-backed WordPress content workflows, package installs, Playground snapshots, and server-side repo primitives; current examples parse a WordPress deploy tree, write/read HEAD plus deployment branch refs, inspect packed branch/tag refs, parse protocol v2 ls-refs discovery responses, build a shallow blobless ref-in-want fetch request, parse protocol v2 fetch response sections and sideband pack/progress/error bytes, orchestrate a protocol v1 send-pack flow from advertised refs through generated branch/tag pack request and status response, build thin REF_DELTA send-pack payloads against remote WordPress base objects, run receive-pack handshake/request/response cycles over native stream, git-daemon, smart HTTP auth/session/redirect, and SSH command adapters, resolve loose+packed refs, locate compacted object offsets through pack indexes and multi-pack-indexes, use MIDX-backed object database pack selection/de-duplication, read delta-resolved packed commit/blob objects, track blobless partial-clone promisor state for omitted media objects, lazily hydrate promised media objects into loose storage, apply sparse checkout materialization to a plugin-focused WordPress tree, recursively merge nested WordPress metadata/theme blobs with Git index v2 conflict-stage writes, checkout-clean merged worktree marker-file output, stale file removal, .git metadata preservation, directory-file tree-stage index expansion, exact same-object rename/delete and rename/rename conflicts, bounded similar-blob rename/delete and rename/modify conflicts for renamed plugin entry files, same-target rename content merges at the renamed plugin path, bounded directory rename/modify merges for renamed plugin directories, directory rename heuristics that match renamed plugin entry files, and pack+loose+alternate object database traversal with replacement refs without shelling out to git.
